## Summary

The degradation is concentrated on the **travelPlan** endpoints. The root cause is in the outbound call from **`ts-travel-plan-service`** (pod `ts-travel-plan-service-b49559b55-7wpck`) to **`ts-seat-service`** (`POST /api/v1/seatservice/seats/left_tickets`). Each of those calls takes about 2.3 seconds of extra time that is not spent in seat-service. I found one primary fault. The other slowdowns look like secondary effects.

## Affected endpoints

| Caller → endpoint | Normal avg | Abnormal avg | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-ui-dashboard / loadgenerator `POST /travelPlan/minStation` | ~0.4–0.7 s | ~14–16 s | 3 errors in 7 loadgen calls |
| `POST /travelPlan/quickest` | ~0.4 s | ~12–13 s | |
| `POST /travelPlan/cheapest` | ~0.4 s | ~12 s | |
| `POST /travel2service/trips/left` | ~0.1 s | ~0.5 s | secondary |
| `POST /preserveservice/preserve` | ~0.26 s | ~0.41 s | secondary |

Loadgenerator and ui-dashboard both show the same 12–19 s latency, so the user-visible impact matches the travel-plan path. Logs for this window are mostly background noise. Some verification-code warnings and food/notification errors show up in both normal and abnormal periods.

- **Primary fault: travel-plan's outbound path to seat-service.** The edge `ts-travel-plan-service → ts-seat-service` has these properties:
  - Client-side span average is about 2365 ms. The seat-service server-side span is about 40 ms.
  - The gap is about 2325 ms on all 146 calls. In normal traffic the gap is about 4 ms.
  - The minimum client duration is 2322 ms, so the delay is consistent rather than occasional.
  - Every one of these calls comes from pod `ts-travel-plan-service-b49559b55-7wpck` to seat pod `ts-seat-service-7b7c5f5d7d-dhxw5`.
  - The only SEVERE log in the dataset is from that same travel-plan pod: `I/O error on POST … seatservice/seats/left_tickets: Connection reset`.
- **Why the seat service is not the origin:** seat-service's own work is normal at about 40 ms. Its leaf spans are sub-millisecond. Other callers of the same seat pod (travel-service and travel2-service) see only about 3–4 ms of gap. The fault is therefore specific to the travel-plan caller pod's connection to seat, not to seat itself.
- **Propagation:** each travelPlan request makes several sequential `left_tickets` calls. Those stalls accumulate into the 12–19 s controller time in travel-plan. That time is then passed upstream to ui-dashboard and loadgenerator.

## Secondary observations

- Route-plan, travel, travel2, basic, and preserve each show only about 5–20 ms of extra gap on their edges, and their leaf spans are fast. This looks like spillover from the load on the travel-plan path, not a separate fault.
- Pod CPU and memory limit utilization are normal or lower during the incident. Container restarts are zero across the services I checked. So this is not resource exhaustion or a crash loop.

## Limits

The telemetry localizes the fault to the travel-plan caller pod's outbound connection to seat. It does not show whether the cause is inside the HTTP client pool, a network path issue, or a retry or timeout setting. A pod-level check on `7wpck` (client connection pool, retries, and network to `dhxw5`) would confirm which one.
